name: Scholarly Growth Separated Review Audit Reputation Qualification
text: Trovò and Massari provide a concrete but partial analogue for the claimed institutional assembly. Ants-Review separates issuers, peer reviewers, approvers, and community contributors; stores the paper and each submitted review on IPFS with hashes recorded on Ethereum; keeps reviewer recommendations and author replies permanently accessible; and lets an approver accept a review and set its reward according to assessed quality. The authors also treat review work as a source of community reputation and propose community voting over review quality. This supports the feasibility of separating production from review while preserving an auditable record and attaching later reputational consequences. It does not, however, bind final judgment to accumulated standing, and its community-voting automation is future work rather than a demonstrated mechanism. The paper therefore qualifies the full architecture rather than validating it.
scope_conditions: The response is limited to the four page-bound passages and the one mapped Kaal claim.
External evidence level: peer-reviewed Euro-Par workshop chapter with a public eight-page arXiv full text and independent Crossref, OpenAlex, and arXiv identity checks.

Ants-Review is a scientific peer-review protocol, not an autonomous-agent validation pool.
The implemented approver accepts reviews and assigns rewards; approval is not weighted by accumulated reputation or standing.
Community upvote/downvote validation and automated payout are described as future development, not demonstrated production behavior.
The evidence supports separation, inspectable records, quality assessment, and reputation-building consequences, but not Kaal's complete adversarial adjudication architecture.
